---
title: "Blinking an LED on the Breadboard"
unit: 3
cluster: "Programming the Board"
---

A program can switch any component we wire to a GPIO pin, not only the
board's own LED. To blink an LED on the breadboard, we connect it to a GPIO
pin instead of the `+` rail.

In this chapter, we'll learn how to:

- connect an LED on the breadboard to a GPIO pin
- blink it with a program

## Connecting the LED to D15

Start with the LED circuit we built on the breadboard, with the board as the
power source. Unplug the USB cable. Then:

1. Remove the blue jumper wire between the `+` rail and `a23`.
2. Connect `a7`, below D15, to `a23` with a new jumper wire, shown in yellow.

![The LED circuit, with its anode connected to D15 by a yellow jumper wire, instead of to the `+` rail. Board photo: PCBCupid.](../images/glyph-c6-breadboard-d15.svg)

The `+` and `−` rails stay connected to 3V3 and GND. The LED's anode now gets
its voltage from GPIO15, through the yellow wire, and its cathode still
returns to GND through the resistor and the `−` rail.

::: {.callout-warning}
Keep the resistor in series with the LED. A GPIO pin can supply much less
current than 3V3, and without the resistor, the LED can draw more than the
pin can safely give. The pin can be damaged without any sign.
:::

## Running the program

Plug the USB cable back in, connect Thonny to the board, and type the blink
program in the editor, with GPIO15 instead of GPIO14:

```python
from machine import Pin
import time

led = Pin(15, Pin.OUT)

delay = 0.5

while True:
    led.on()
    time.sleep(delay)
    led.off()
    time.sleep(delay)
```

Click Run. The LED on the breadboard blinks, and the board's own LED stays as
it is, because the program no longer switches GPIO14. A program switches the
pin we give it, and only what is connected to that pin.

## Summary

A program blinks an LED on the breadboard through the GPIO pin it is wired
to, while the rails keep supplying power to the rest of the circuit.

| Connection or code       | What it does |
|--------------------------|--------------|
| 3V3 → `+` rail, GND → `−` rail | supply power whenever the board is plugged in |
| D15 → LED anode          | lets the program switch the LED |
| `led = Pin(15, Pin.OUT)` | sets up GPIO15 as an output |
| `led.on()`, `led.off()`  | switch GPIO15, and the LED connected to it |
| Resistor in series       | limits the current the GPIO pin has to supply |
